approach: `take_baseline` (run/checks.rs) first looks for a green GitHub run of the base's governed content, then falls back to today's local run. It looks only in a non-nested job whose origin is a github.com https URL. It makes at most two lookups, each one read with no wait and an `Exec` that refuses to run checks. Both go through the candidate path unchanged: `routing::route`, `routing::run_routed_with_record`, `ci_result::resolve`. Lookup A (the landed candidate's run, matched by fingerprint) reads only main's own tree. The base is a squash commit. A post-C0 landing commit carries its job's closing records under `records/jobs/<month>/<id>/` (`gh/landing.rs:55-75` `landed_commit_from_records` reads `<job dir>/verification.json` from a commit on main; `athena-gate/src/invariant.rs:240-268` `closing_jobs` finds a landing by the 'A' diff entries of those files). So A diffs the base's single parent against the base and finds the one job whose `verification.json` was added. It parses that file as `athena_data::records::Verification` and accepts it only if `verified_fingerprint == fingerprint(&git, base, base)`. It then resolves `candidate_commit` on `gh::ci_branch(job)`, passing the squash's changed paths as `changed`. That keeps the workflow-changed guard in `resolve` (ci_result.rs:222-225) live. Lookup B is the base SHA on the host's default branch, read locally from `origin/HEAD`; this is main's push run. A hit is a `Source::Ci` record with `all_passed()`; the baseline then holds the reused `CheckRun`s and a new optional `Baseline.reused_from` (the run address). Anything else runs `baseline_checks` as today. The reason is printed on a `ci         baseline ...` line. No refusal or matching rule of the reading/plan kind is added or changed (the fingerprint comparison is an equality guard), so no refusal_corpus case applies and I name none.

decisions.choice: Lookup A reads the landed job's closing records from main's tree: diff the base's single parent to the base, take the one added `records/jobs/<month>/<id>/verification.json`, parse it as `Verification`, and compare `verified_fingerprint` with `fingerprint(&git, base, base)`. Then resolve `candidate_commit` on `ci_branch(job)`. B follows: the base SHA on the default branch.
decisions.reason: This answers round-2 finding 3. A post-C0 landed commit carries the job's closing records in its own tree. `landed_commit_from_records` (gh/landing.rs:55-75) reads `<job dir>/verification.json` from a commit on main. `closing_jobs` (invariant.rs:240-268) and the pre-merge rule (invariant.rs:643-710) require `candidate.json`, `verification.json` and the landed `outcome.json` to be added by the landing commit and to hold the landed fingerprint. Reading the base's own tree needs no records branch, no new athena-gate function and no invented record location. The squash also names the changed paths (finding 4). Fingerprint equality using `fingerprint(&git, base, base)` (the call candidate.rs:37 uses for `base_fingerprint`) is the 'same governed content' guard. `resolve` keeps its exact-SHA check (ci_result.rs:196), so only a run of `candidate_commit` can pass.

rejected.option: Read the landing record on `athena/records` and a `verification.json` from that branch (round-2 plan)
rejected.why: Round-2 finding 3: no production code writes or reads a job's verification on the records tip; only history records (landings, landing-intents) live there. The test would have passed on records the plan invented.

rejected.option: Lookup B only (SHA on the default branch)
rejected.why: Main's push run for the squash is often unfinished while the next job starts, so the saving would rarely appear, and the request names the landed candidate's run.

rejected.option: A new CI lookup or an index of runs by fingerprint
rejected.why: Criterion 5 asks for the existing `resolve` path.

rejected.option: Also require `final_verdict == Pass` and a landed `outcome.json` in the base tree
rejected.why: The evidence is the green CI run of `candidate_commit` plus equal governed content. The landing check (invariant.rs:683-710) already refused any other squash at merge. Extra reads and parsing add code without adding trust.

decisions.choice: Pass the squash's changed paths (the diff entries other than the closing records file) as `changed` to lookup A. Pass `&[]` to lookup B.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 4. `resolve` distrusts a green run when `changed` has a path under `.github/workflows/` (ci_result.rs:222-225), because the candidate controlled the checker that produced the run. A previous job that edited a workflow gets a refusal from `resolve`; the refusing `Exec` turns the fallback into an error, and the stage runs locally. Lookup B's SHA is the merged base itself, not an unverified candidate, so the guard does not apply.

rejected.option: Read the previous candidate record's change list
rejected.why: The candidate's commit and record are not in main's tree under a fixed shape; the squash diff is local, certain and conservative.

decisions.choice: Lookup B's branch is the default branch read from the local `origin/HEAD`, using the existing `local_default_branch` in reconcile.rs:370 made `pub(crate)`. With `origin/HEAD` unset, lookup B is skipped and the reason line says so. `git.current_branch()` is not used.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 6. Main's push run is on the default branch, which is where `land` merges (gh/landing.rs:414 uses `host.default_branch()`). The checkout may be detached or on another branch. A local read needs no host call, so the baseline can never fail because of it.

rejected.why: A detached HEAD or a feature branch gives none or the wrong branch for main's run.
An extra API call in a stage that must stay cheap, and `with_ci_source_on` gives the closure only a `CiSource`, not the client.
A second copy of the same reader; a one-word visibility change is smaller.

decisions.choice: Add `reused_from: Option<String>` to `Baseline` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; the schema tag stays `athena.baseline/1`.
decisions.reason: Old files parse. Local-baseline files are byte-identical to before. `check_record_file`, the path allow-list and the `AnyRecord::Baseline` arm need no change.

rejected.why: Needs a new tag and allow-list work, and old files would stop parsing unchanged.

decisions.choice: The fallback reason goes on the output line `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>`, not into `Baseline.note`. This departs from the wording of criterion 2 ('also leaves a note'); the producer's report must say so.
decisions.reason: `Baseline::failed_before` and `failed_tests_before` return nothing whenever `note` is set (records.rs:2629-2644). A note on a local fallback would stop real pre-existing failures from being excused. That changes the verdict rules, which are out of scope.

rejected.option: Set `Baseline.note` on a red or error lookup
rejected.why: It would disable pre-existing-failure marking for that job.

decisions.choice: Use `routing::route(Some("config"), ctx.capability.checks(jc), &[])`, a refusing `Exec`, and `Wait{polls:1, pause:0}`. Run the lookups only when `route.reuse` is true.
decisions.reason: `Kind::parse` maps an unknown kind to `config`, for which `path_rule_applies` is false (routing.rs:48-63), so no check is skipped and the reused baseline has the same checks a local one has. `resolve` falls back to its `LocalChecks` when there is no green run. The refusing `Exec` turns that into an `Err`, which the stage reads as 'no usable result'. A `Red` result returns `Ok` with `!all_passed()` and is also treated as no reuse. Waiting or polling would be new behavior.

rejected.option: Call `resolve` directly and rebuild the runs

rejected.why: Path skipping needs a change list, and the baseline has none (records.rs:2616).

risks.risk: The landing is a squash of several jobs' records, or a rebased squash, so lookup A finds zero or several verification files.
risks.mitigation: Exactly one added verification file is required, as the pre-merge rule requires one job per commit (records-history.md:318-319). Otherwise A is skipped, B runs, then the local run, with the reason printed. No job fails because of the lookup.

risks.risk: GitHub drops the runs of a deleted CI branch (the branch is deleted when the job closes, gh/early.rs:334-335), or its `branch` filter fails for it, so lookup A never hits live.
risks.mitigation: A falls back to B and then to a local run. This is the first Host question. The producer's tests use the fake and do not prove live behavior.

risks.risk: A kind that applies the path rule could skip checks, so a reused baseline would hold fewer checks than a local one.
risks.mitigation: The `config` kind applies no path skipping and the change list for the route is empty. The criterion 1 tests assert the three check names.

risks.risk: A fingerprint match is wrongly trusted when the rules differ. The recorded `verified_fingerprint` was computed as `fingerprint(&git, &c, &p)`, the candidate's content under the previous job's base rules `p` (candidate.rs:170, mod.rs:542). It is compared with `fingerprint(&git, base, base)`, the base's content under the base's own rules.
risks.mitigation: The comparison is conservative. If the previous job changed the rules (athena.toml or .gitattributes), the hashes differ, A is refused and the job runs locally: safe, with no saving. The criterion 2 loop includes a mismatched fingerprint. The squash's changed paths are passed to `resolve`, so a workflow edit also refuses a green run.

risks.risk: Extra reads and git work on every GitHub-origin job, and a read error breaking the baseline stage.
risks.mitigation: At most two reads, no pause. `read_ci` turns a fetch error into Missing (ci_result.rs:192). Any `Err` from the git reads, the parse or the routed call is caught and becomes a fallback reason. `take_baseline` still never fails.

risks.risk: A green run of `candidate_commit` stands in for a baseline of the base, which is a rebased version of the same content.
risks.mitigation: The guard is equality of the governed-content fingerprint, the same notion candidate reuse relies on. `resolve` still requires the run's SHA to equal the one asked for.

risks.risk: `origin/HEAD` is unset on the operator's machine, so lookup B never runs.
risks.mitigation: A still runs and the fallback is the local run. The reason line says `origin/HEAD is not set`. See the second Host question.

risks.risk: An older Athena binary reads a reused baseline under `deny_unknown_fields`.
risks.mitigation: `skip_serializing_if` keeps local-baseline files unchanged. Only a reused baseline carries the key, and records are read by the same release.

demonstrations.method: Two whole-job tests through `Athena::go`. (a) `baseline_reused_from_landed_candidate_run_runs_nothing_locally`: a helper commits a squash whose parent-to-commit diff adds the closing `verification.json` of a previous job, written with the production `Verification` type at its canonical path. Its `verified_fingerprint` is the real `fingerprint(git, base, base)`, and its `candidate_commit` is a known SHA. The fake answers a green run only for that SHA on `athena/ci/<prev job>` and an empty list for the base SHA on the default branch. (b) `baseline_reused_from_main_run_runs_nothing_locally`: no landed squash; `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` points at `origin/main`; the fake answers green for the base SHA on `main` only.
demonstrations.observes: In both tests the stored baseline (`baseline.json` in the job dir, read through the records) has `reused_from == Some(CI_RUN_ADDRESS)`, `note` None, and checks fmt, clippy and test, each `reused` true and `passed` true with a note naming the CI run and the SHA it ran for. The file `<job_dir>/baseline-ran` does not exist. The check-executor seam recorded no baseline probe. The output holds `ci         baseline reused from <CI_RUN_ADDRESS> for <base>`. In (a) `baseline_reads()` shows one read, on `athena/ci/<prev job>` with `head_sha` equal to the previous candidate's SHA.
